source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Across the 250-household survey, farmers had an average total landholding of about 3.72 hectares (ranging from as little as 0.20 ha to as much as 44 ha). Landholding was often split into multiple plots: 100 households had a first plot averaging 2.88 ha (range 0.15-30 ha); 27 households additionally had a second plot averaging 2.30 ha (range 0.10-30 ha); and 10 households had a third plot averaging 2.11 ha (range 0.20-15 ha).

Average years of experience growing corn specifically was 4.65 years (range 2-28 years), and average land area planted to corn (as opposed to total household landholding) was 2.68 hectares (range 1-22 ha). Female-headed households averaged smaller corn plots at 1.41 hectares (range 1-6 ha, based on 87 female-headed households in the sample). Households where the head had less than 18 years of general life/farming experience averaged 1.69 hectares under corn (range 1-7 ha, 13 households).

Province-level average landholding and per-hectare production cost varied substantially: Kampong Cham households averaged 3.14 ha of land with a production cost of about 2,190,335 riel/ha; Kandal averaged 1.23 ha at about 2,737,039 riel/ha (the highest per-hectare cost of the four); Battambang averaged 6.09 ha (largest average holding) at about 1,391,177 riel/ha; and Pailin averaged 4.44 ha at about 1,130,290 riel/ha (the lowest per-hectare cost).
